requirements.HFO01: Up to 128 cached snapshot generations, retaining the existing 128 MiB weighted budget per process/engine; numeric buffers counted by nbytes plus conservative map/grid overhead.
requirements.HFO02: Immutable bytes-backed uint32 ticks and uint64 cumulative counts; zero-copy derived frequencies. Format3 omits duplicate persisted counts, preserving an empty compatibility field. Actual format2 reader and population class read format3 correctly.
requirements.HFO03: Both live personal PBs are selected in one bounded UNION ALL query. Private ETags include identity, scope, generation, live PBs and every requested frame/candidate/bin input. Visibility/auth precede 304; existing native client already supports conditional GET.
requirements.HFO04: Indexed durable demand tracks recently viewed board/car/scope without player IDs. Coalesce 60s/5s when unavailable, cap 4096 local keys and 16 pending notes, expire interest after10min. Read transaction releases its connection before best-effort demand persistence. Active refresh selects one due interest before snapshot joins, bounds expiry deletion to100, and retains token fences. Service reserves a turn each16 completed jobs; requested historical lap prerequisites use at most two board PKs and200 attempts per turn.
requirements.HFO05: Offline prefix prototype batches all boundary nodes in one indexed query. Exact agreement for ordinary public fields; retained orphan lap and cross-board duplicate cases demonstrate production eligibility/dedup mismatch. Prototype remains disabled in production.
requirements.R01: Preserve authoritative results, exact snapshot counts/ties, public/development isolation, publication state, account/visibility checks, leases, resets and recovery. Preserve concurrent edits.
requirements.Q01: Actual selected SQLite/PostgreSQL, native packet, rolling-reader and synthetic measurement receipts. No assertions removed or weakened.

limits: Synthetic weighted counts do not establish 500M-account or1M-DAU production capacity. Measure full HTTP throughput, DB I/O, peak memory and concurrent cold misses on representative infrastructure.

Cached default grids cost O(B); custom frames O(B log U); cold snapshot transfer/packing O(U). The single personal query uses indexed player/board keys. Large flying-lap and deduplicated development refreshes retain SQL grouping proportional to PB population, potentially O(N log N) if a plan sorts or spills. Prefix reuse is not safe for those eligibility rules yet.

128MiB is an estimated weighted snapshot cache allowance per process, not total RSS. At most128 entries remain subject to that allowance; full-domain fields hit the byte budget sooner. Transient JSON/packing allocations and other application caches are additional.

Frequency JSON reduced20.1% and cache weight estimate87.5% in the216000-distinct-time synthetic probe. Packed bin calculation was about11 microseconds slower in that desktop benchmark; no raw bin CPU speedup is claimed.

Demand reads are bounded but require a small coalesced after-response write; notes are best effort and finite TTL. Brief missed notes retry on later reads. A reserved turn can occupy a worker while SQL refresh runs; production latency and worker count need measurement.
Existing population-based refresh lag and prior large-field one-place self-correction approximation remain; counts within a snapshot stay exact. This task adds no intentional count approximation.
